items.title: Language Models Can Rewrite Their Own Weights

extra.evidence: A language model is trained once and frozen. Making it better takes another training run, or a prompt, a harness or extra computation at inference that is gone once the task ends. We show a third way: to our knowledge for the first time, a language model rewrites its own weights by its own reasoning and becomes better, with no gradients and no training. We call this self-rewriting: the model is its own optimizer. In earlier work, a frontier model edited a much smaller one; here an open 27B model, given its weights, its graded answers and the ability to run itself, diagnoses its own failure and rewrites the weights behind it. It surpasses itself: its own edit makes it 6.6 points more accurate on problems it never saw. It keeps getting better: it tests its edits on practice problems and sub…

items.title: 黎曼猜想被证明？！Claude加持，34岁数学家放出Lean证明

items.title: Accelerate Bench: Evaluating Agents for Application-Level Program Optimization
items.summary: Application optimization requires coding agents to discover useful changes and coordinate them across a complete program while preserving the required computation. We introduce Accelerate Bench, a benchmark of 32 CPU optimization tasks adapted from scientific applications and supercomputing competitions. Each task provides a working program and specifies the workload, correctness requirements, timing boundaries, and permitted edits, leaving agents to choose where and how to optimize. Public testing supports iterative development, and a separate verifier scores the final submission. On benchmark version 1.1, we evaluate 16 coding agents, each pairing a model with a harness. Their Score@1 ranges from 25.5% to 67.4%. Most of their programs are correct, and the size of the speedup separates them: the two leading agents are at least 2x faster on 22 or more of the 32 tasks, while the other fourteen reach 2x on 8 to 17 and leave 125 of their 412 correct outcomes below 1.25x. Controlled replays show why coordination across an application matters: identical source code runs between 0.29x and 2.12x depending only on build and runtime settings, and one code change is worth 1.01x or 6.4x depending on another. Accelerate Bench pairs executable workloads with agents' programs and trajectories to evaluate both their gains and the process behind them.
items.title_zh: Accelerate Bench：应用级程序优化智能体评测
items.summary_zh: 为解决应用级程序优化中智能体发现有用变更并协调完整程序的问题，论文提出了 Accelerate Bench 基准。该基准包含 32 个 CPU 优化任务，评估了 16 个编码智能体。结果显示，智能体在 32 个任务上的 Score@1 范围为 25.5% 到 67.4%，领先者至少在 22 个任务上实现 2 倍加速。

items.title: MemFolder: Structure-Guided Memory Folding for Efficient Agent Memory Management
items.summary: Long-term agents accumulate large external memory stores as interactions unfold, increasing the costs of storage, retrieval, and response generation. Efficiency is constrained by two coupled factors: a growing record count increases retrieval overhead, while longer retrieved contexts increase prefill computation and decoding-time attention costs. Existing methods prune or consolidate records, but pruning can discard useful evidence, whereas consolidation may produce fewer yet longer retrieval units. We introduce MemFolder, a structure-guided memory folding framework that sequentially reduces record count and context length. The framework comprises two core components that share memory groups, using cross-record structure to guide both evidence consolidation and compact representation. RecordFolder grounds entity mentions, progressively selects representative yet complementary anchors, and combines semantic and entity affinity with temporal chaining to consolidate compatible records into fewer retrieval units. ContextFolder encodes the original records within these groups into compact text and uses verification feedback to revise encodings when key facts cannot be recovered. Experiments on the three text-based memory benchmarks LoCoMo, PersonaMem, and LongMemEval and the two multimodal benchmarks M3-Bench-web and M3-Bench-robot demonstrate the strong performance of our methods. Notably, on Mem0, RecordFolder retains 99.0% of the original average performance across the three t…
items.summary_zh: 为解决长期智能体记忆管理中存储、检索和响应生成成本增加的问题，论文提出了 MemFolder 框架。该框架通过 RecordFolder 和 ContextFolder 两个组件，利用跨记录结构引导证据整合和紧凑表示。实验表明，该方法在多个基准上表现良好，在 Mem0 上保持了 99.0% 的原始平均性能。

items.title: NariQ: Sub-3-Bit Quantization for Long-Horizon Agentic Tasks
items.summary: Long-horizon agentic tasks require a model to call tools over many steps at contexts of 100K tokens or more, yet many low-bit quantization methods are calibrated on short web text and judged on perplexity. This mismatch is costly: existing quantizations of Qwen3.8-27B at or below 3 bits per weight match BF16 on shorter tasks like AIME, yet in published results solve at most 72% as many tasks as BF16 on DeepSWE, a long-horizon agentic benchmark. We propose NariQ, a trellis-coded post-training quantization method that calibrates on tokens generated by the BF16 model in agent sessions. On Qwen3.8-27B, NariQ at 3.0 and 2.5 bits per weight stays level with BF16 on two long-horizon agentic benchmarks, DeepSWE and Terminal Bench, as well as on AIME and RealWorldQA. Our checkpoint at 2.0 bits per weight trails this performance. To our knowledge, these are the first quantizations at or below 3 bits per weight shown to match their full-precision version on long-horizon agentic tasks. We release the files as Qwen3.8-27B-NariQ-GGUF (https://huggingface.co/nari-labs/Qwen3.8-27B-NariQ-GGUF), with inference available through our llama.cpp fork at https://github.com/nari-labs/nari-llama.cpp.
items.title_zh: NariQ：长时序智能任务的亚 3 位量化
items.summary_zh: 为解决长时序智能任务中低比特量化方法在长上下文下性能下降的问题，论文提出了 NariQ 方法。该方法在 Qwen3.8-27B 模型上实现了 3.0 和 2.5 位权重的量化，在 DeepSWE 和 Terminal Bench 等长时序智能基准上与 BF16 性能持平。这是首次在长时序智能任务中展示的亚 3 位量化方法。

items.title: WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent for Omni AI-Generated Video Detection
items.summary: Recent advances in video generation call for reliable detection grounded in explicit forensic evidence. However, current methods primarily depend on single-pass chain-of-thought reasoning that overlooks brief or localized artifacts, or on predefined multi-agent workflows that offer limited flexibility in selecting relevant inspections. Even with adaptive investigation, optimizing the investigation policy alone does not directly improve the forensic capabilities of fixed experts. We introduce WeVisForensics, an agentic framework in which a main investigator agent coordinates a self-evolving library of forensic inspector sub-agents spanning visual and audio cues. The investigator learns which artifact type to examine, over which window, and when to conclude, and these interactions provide shared feedback for both levels of agents. Our dual-timescale policy optimization strategy, DTPO, closes this loop through fast reinforcement learning of the investigator and slower refinement of the inspectors, guided by annotated artifact intervals, to report subtle artifacts they once dismissed. Furthermore, we curate ForenCue-30K, combining role-specific forensic annotations and interaction trajectories to supervise individual inspections and their coordination, with an accompanying reinforcement-learning pool. Experiments show that WeVisForensics averages 95.2% detection accuracy across in-domain, out-of-domain and agentic benchmarks, 9.0% above the strongest prior detector, while ground…

items.title: Sightline: Long-Window Speculative Decoding for Fast SVG Generation
items.summary: Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) generation models write a graphic as code with one forward pass per token, so drawing is slow. Speculative decoding speeds them up losslessly, and block drafters guess many tokens per pass. On SVG, many of their rounds accept the whole draft and end only at the verification window. We find that their misses are rare and clumped, and that they stay accurate far deeper into a block than on natural language. A run-length identity and three propositions show that a longer window pays once the candidates are wide, up to the drafter's horizon. We propose Sightline, which pairs a window as long as the drafter's horizon with a draft tree wide enough to fill it. Experiments cover text-to-SVG and image-to-SVG with three models on six benchmarks from MMSVG, MMSVG-2M and SArena. In every setting, Sightline is the fastest of the compared lossless decoders. On SArena, it stays the fastest when every decoder shares one loop control. It also leads in almost every setting of six models from four other families, which write SVG code, compressed SVG tokens or Lottie JSON. Analyses trace the lead to rounds that shorter windows cut off, both in loop-free content and in loops. Speculative decoding also saves time for choosing samples by rendering, which beats choosing by likelihood. These results suggest that speculative decoding on vector graphics should verify as far as the drafter sees. Code and data are available at https://github.com/LiZaiyuan0619/Sightline.
items.title_zh: Sightline：SVG 生成的高速长窗口推测解码
items.summary_zh: 为解决 SVG 生成模型因逐 token 前向传播导致的速度慢问题，论文提出了 Sightline 方法。该方法通过长窗口与宽草稿树的结合，在 MMSVG、SArena 等六个基准上实现了最快的无损解码速度。实验表明，推测解码在矢量图形上应验证到草稿者的视野范围。

12a96840525c.body: METR 报告更新了时间跨度图，指出部分 AI 能力呈指数级提升，但模型在需要判断的任务上不如编程任务表现好。

550ba5112f8b.headline: 黎曼猜想被证明
550ba5112f8b.body: 34 岁数学家 Levent Alpöge 与 Claude 合作，发布了黎曼猜想的 Lean 形式化证明代码。

d941cdc9a6e3.headline: autoclip：开源 AI 视频剪辑工具
d941cdc9a6e3.body: 开源 AI 视频剪辑工具，一键将长视频剪成短视频并生成字幕。

524fb8fc2e36.headline: vLLM 原生支持 Inkling 2 Mini
524fb8fc2e36.body: vLLM 原生支持 Thinking Machines 的 Inkling 2 Mini，这是一种循环 MoE 模型。

b9a1ff778498.headline: neonclipping：本地开源剪辑引擎
b9a1ff778498.body: 本地开源剪辑引擎，粘贴链接即可在约 2 分钟内生成带字幕的 9:16 短视频。

7610dae89799.headline: agentscope：构建可理解可信任的智能体
7610dae89799.body: agentscope 是一个用于构建和运行智能体的框架。

eb91946ecbe1.headline: linger：完全在本地运行的个人 AI 代理
eb91946ecbe1.body: 完全在本地运行的个人 AI 代理，旨在打破科技巨头对 AI 的控制。

ace09be0a9c3.headline: jan：完全离线的 ChatGPT 开源替代品
ace09be0a9c3.body: 完全离线的 ChatGPT 开源替代品，可在本地电脑运行。

420e52b47a4c.headline: app-store-compliance：开源应用商店合规指南
420e52b47a4c.body: 开源指南，包含 117 种常见应用商店拒绝模式及修复方案。

295fc122b36a.headline: Dify 发布 1.20.0 版本
295fc122b36a.body: Dify 1.20.0 支持导出追踪数据到 OpenTelemetry 收集器，并扫描知识库文件中的恶意软件。

51bab1455c66.headline: Accelerate Bench：应用级程序优化智能体评测
51bab1455c66.body: 论文提出了 Accelerate Bench 基准，包含 32 个 CPU 优化任务，评估了 16 个编码智能体。

585e3c3f7fab.headline: MemFolder：结构引导的记忆折叠
585e3c3f7fab.body: 论文提出了 MemFolder 框架，通过 RecordFolder 和 ContextFolder 组件解决长期智能体记忆管理问题。

7c178d59a2a5.headline: NariQ：长时序智能任务的亚3位量化
7c178d59a2a5.body: 论文提出NariQ方法，在Qwen3.8-27B模型上实现3.0和2.5位权重量化，在长时序智能基准上与BF16性能持平。

044cbece4c9d.headline: WeVisForensics：全AI生成视频检测的进化智能体
044cbece4c9d.body: 论文提出WeVisForensics框架，包含主调查智能体和自进化检测子智能体库，在多个基准上的检测准确率达到95.2%。

783b22effef8.headline: Sightline：SVG生成的高速长窗口推测解码
783b22effef8.body: 论文提出Sightline方法，通过长窗口与宽草稿树结合，在MMSVG、SArena等六个基准上实现了最快的无损解码速度。
